problem: The copyable command calls bare `pytest`. This is a uv project: the tools live in the uv-managed environment, so a contributor who hasn't activated it gets 'command not found', or runs a different pytest. CONTRIBUTING and the project's own instructions use `uv run pytest --cov=src/pyeye`.
subject: run `pytest --cov=src/pyeye --cov-report=term`

problem: The section's ruff commands (C90, PLR0913, PLR0912) call bare `ruff`, which is only installed in the uv-managed environment. The same applies to each of them.
replacement: Prefix each command with `uv run`, e.g. run `uv run ruff check --select C90 <changed_files>` (and likewise for PLR0913 and PLR0912).
subject: run `ruff check --select C90 <changed_files>`

problem: The command calls bare `ruff`, which is only installed in the uv-managed environment.
subject: run `ruff check --select PLR2004 <changed_files>`

problem: Nothing backs the 50-line limit: no tool or config in the repo measures it. pyproject's ruff `select` doesn't enable C90/PLR rules at all, so every threshold in this checklist is a convention only. The other items at least name the ruff rule that defines their limit. This one is a bare number with no source.
replacement: Either delete the item, or reword it without a figure ("- [ ] No overly long functions; split ones that do more than one thing").
subject: No functions longer than 50 lines (excluding docstrings)

problem: "No code duplication" is absolute, but the ratchet it cites only scans `src/pyeye/mcp/operations/` and `src/pyeye/canonicalization.py` (the hook's `files` filter and the script's default targets). It also passes for baselined clones. Passing it doesn't show the PR adds no duplication elsewhere.
replacement: - [ ] No new copies of existing logic (the `duplicate-code-report` ratchet passes for the MCP operations and canonicalization, where it fails on a new copy; elsewhere, check by review; see `docs/development/duplicate-code-check.md`)
subject: No code duplication (the `duplicate-code-report` ratchet passes

problem: The hook ID `duplicate-code-report` is written by hand. It is a registered repo_config fact, so a renamed hook would leave this checklist item pointing at nothing.
replacement: Bind the hook ID through a fact block for precommit.hook.duplicate-code-report instead of typing it.
